summary: The Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2026 prohibits the Federal Government from acquiring, possessing, accessing, or using biometric surveillance systems and information derived from them, unless explicitly authorized by an Act of Congress. It also makes State and local governments ineligible for certain Byrne grant program funds unless they adopt laws or policies substantially similar to the federal prohibition.

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from acquiring, possessing, accessing, or using biometric surveillance systems and subject to disciplinary penalties or lawsuits for violations.
Must enact laws or policies substantially similar to the federal prohibition in order to remain eligible for Federal Byrne grant program funding.
Gain the right to sue the Federal Government for damages and other relief if their rights are violated by unauthorized biometric surveillance.

key_provisions: Makes it unlawful for any Federal agency or official to acquire, possess, access, or use biometric surveillance systems or information derived from them without explicit statutory authorization.
Sets strict criteria for any future congressional authorization, including privacy protections, minimum accuracy standards, and audit requirements.
Prohibits the Federal Government from using information obtained in violation of this Act in any criminal, civil, or administrative proceeding, except in a proceeding alleging a violation of the Act.

Creates a private right of action allowing injured individuals and State attorneys general to sue the Federal Government for violations, with potential recovery for actual damages, punitive damages, and attorneys' fees.
Subjects federal officials who violate the prohibition to retraining, suspension, termination, or other penalties.
Denies Byrne grant program funding to State and local governments unless they enforce a law or policy substantially similar to the federal biometric surveillance prohibition.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2026 prohibits the Federal Government from acquiring, possessing, accessing, or using biometric surveillance systems and information derived from them, unless explicitly authorized by an Act of Congress. It also makes State and local governments ineligible for certain Byrne grant program funds unless they adopt laws or policies substantially similar to the federal prohibition.
summary_detail.significance: This bill places severe statutory restrictions on the use of facial recognition and other biometric technologies by federal, state, and local governments, impacting law enforcement practices nationwide and creating civil liabilities for unauthorized use.
